arxiv-1811-08105.title: Phase diffusion and the small-noise approximation in linear amplifiers: Limitations and beyond
arxiv-1811-08105.creator: Andy Chia, Michal Hajdušek, Rosario Fazio, Leong-Chuan Kwek, Vlatko Vedral
arxiv-1811-08105.description: Abstract The phase of an optical field inside a linear amplifier is widely known to diffuse with a diffusion coefficient that is inversely proportional to the photon number. The same process occurs in lasers which limits its intrinsic linewidth and makes the phase uncertainty difficult to calculate.

arxiv-2109-01354.description: Abstract A notion of balanced pairs in an extriangulated category with a negative first extension is defined in this article. arxiv-2311-07656.title: Strong size evolution of disc galaxies since z=1 Thanks: Table 1 are only available in electronic form at the CDS via anonymous ftp to cdsarc.u-strasbg.fr (130.79.128.5) or via http://cdsweb.u-strasbg.fr/cgi-bin/qcat?J/A+A/.
arxiv-2311-07656.creator: Fernando Buitrago, Ignacio Trujillo
arxiv-2311-07656.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Fernando Buitrago, Ignacio Trujillo. Our understanding of how the size of galaxies has evolved over cosmic time is based on the use of the half-light (effective) radius as a size indicator. Although the half-light radius has many advantages for structurally parameterising galaxies, it does not provide a measure of the global extent of the objects, but only an indication of the size of the region containing the innermost 50% of the galaxy’s light.

arxiv-2408-07121.title: Quiet Please: Detrending Radial Velocity Variations from Stellar Activity with a Physically Motivated Spot Model
arxiv-2408-07121.creator: Jared C. Siegel, Samuel Halverson, Jacob K. Luhn, Lily L. Zhao, Khaled Al Moulla, Paul Robertson, Chad F. Bender, Ryan C. Terrien, Arpita Roy, Suvrath Mahadevan, Fred Hearty, Joe P. Ninan, Jason T. Wright, Eric B. Ford, Christian Schwab, Guðmundur Stefánsson, Cullen H. Blake, Michael W. McElwain
arxiv-2408-07121.description: Abstract For solar-type stars, spots and their associated magnetic regions induce radial velocity perturbations through the Doppler rotation signal and the suppression of convective blueshift—collectively known as rotation–modulation. We developed the Rotation–Convection (RC) model: a method of detrending and characterizing rotation–modulation, using only cross–correlation functions or 1–dimensional spectra, without the need for continuous high cadence measurements.

pmc-10758861.title: “Pick a Plan and Roll the Dice”: A qualitative study of consumer experiences selecting a health plan in the non-group market
pmc-10758861.creator: Elena Faugno, Melissa B Gilkey, Lauren A Cripps, Anna Sinaiko, Alon Peltz, Jon Kingsdale, Alison A Galbraith
pmc-10758861.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Highlights•We interviewed 36 US adults with negative experiences with non-group insurance plans.•Participants reported facing substantial challenges to choosing an insurance plan.•Barriers included understanding key terms, finding information, and comparing plans.•Consumers of non-group insurance plans desire customized decision support.Keywords: Health plan selection, Insurance marketplace, Consumer decision making, Affordable Care Act, Open enrollment

Introduction

Choosing a health insurance plan can be difficult [1], [2], especially for individuals and families in the non-group (individual) insurance market.

pmc-12475485.title: Diagnostic performance of HIV risk assessment tools for identifying pre-exposure prophylaxis candidates: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12475485.creator: Myo Minn Oo, Monica Rudd, Caley Shukalek, Teruko Kishibe, Mark Hull, Darrell HS Tan
pmc-12475485.description: SummaryBackgroundTo support the implementation of HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis evaluating the diagnostic performance of HIV risk assessment tools in predicting HIV infection.MethodsWe searched MEDLINE, Embase, and CINAHL for observational studies published between January 1, 1998, and May 13, 2024 that reported on the diagnostic performance of HIV risk assessment tools.

pmc-12786576.title: From Pixels to Predictions: Integrating Machine Learning and Digital Image Correlation for Damage Identification in Engineering Materials
pmc-12786576.creator: Mostafa Sadeghian, Arvydas Palevicius, Jokubas Sablinskas, Paulius Griskevicius
pmc-12786576.description: Damage assessment in engineering materials is essential for structural reliability and safety. While traditional imaging techniques and Digital Image Correlation (DIC) provide valuable insights into deformation and crack evolution, they often require significant manual effort and suffer from accuracy limitations under complex loading conditions.

pmc-13083980.title: Remarkable response of metaplastic breast cancer to a novel targeted AKT inhibitor TAS-117 in a Cowden syndrome patient: a case report
pmc-13083980.creator: Eva Godina, Marta Fernández Carcaño, Burak Uzunparmak, Thomas Pepper, Pooja Shah, Jordi Rodon
pmc-13083980.description: PTEN hamartoma tumour syndrome (PHTS) is characterized by a germline PTEN mutation and a substantial increase in lifetime breast cancer risk to 85% with lower age at first diagnosis. Despite the availability of agents targeting PTEN-regulated PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway, there are currently no approved treatments for PHTS patients with cancer.

pmc-13106827.title: Not all task-unrelated thoughts (TUT) are created equal - TUT characteristics as predictors of affective states and heart-rate variability
pmc-13106827.creator: Michał S Skorupski, Izabela Krejtz, Steven Barnes, Celine Baeyens, Thierry Atzeni, Monika Kornacka
pmc-13106827.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Task-Unrelated Thoughts (TUT) are a prevalent transdiagnostic phenomenon, robustly associated with both adaptive and maladaptive outcomes. However, it is still not clear which factors determine the maladaptive outcomes of TUT. In this study, we focused on analysing the role of a wide spectrum of TUT characteristics in everyday functioning, specifically their associations with momentary affective states, depressive symptoms, heart rate variability, and sleep quality.

pmc-13178655.title: Towards precision medicine for brain arteriovenous malformations
pmc-13178655.creator: Andrew T. Hale, Adam J. Kundishora, Pazhanichamy Kalailingam, Tanyeri Barak, Phan Q. Duy, Christopher M. Ramundo, Baojian Fan, Qiang Li, Priscilla K. Brastianos, Ganesh M. Shankar, Seth L. Alper, Benjamin P. Kleinstiver, Patricia L. Musolino, Kristopher T. Kahle
pmc-13178655.description: Recent advances in cerebrovascular genomics, single-cell biology, pharmacology, and gene editing technology are transforming our understanding of brain arteriovenous malformations (bAVMs) — a leading cause of pediatric hemorrhagic stroke. Once considered static anatomical defects, bAVMs are now recognized as dynamic, genetically driven lesions resulting from somatic mutations in KRAS, BRAF, and pathways involved in arteriovenous specification, angiogenesis, and vascular remodeling.

pmc-13508519.title: Ultrabroadband Multiplex CARS Imaging Reveals Distinct Protein- and Lipid-Rich Domains in Arbuscules
pmc-13508519.creator: Amu Sofue, Naoya Takeda, Shinsuke Shigeto
pmc-13508519.description: Arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) fungi form mutualistic symbioses with a wide range of terrestrial plants, in which they exchange inorganic nutrients taken up from the soil for plant-derived photosynthates such as sugars and lipids. This nutrient exchange occurs exclusively at arbusculeshighly branched hyphal structures that develop in the plant root cortex.
